notes: Relationships are directed and each includes an explanatory description.
Claims explicitly uncertain or marked citation-needed in the supplied source are qualified in descriptions.
Release facts reflect the supplied article's stated snapshot and have not been independently refreshed.

entities.name: Perl
entities.description: High-level, general-purpose, interpreted, dynamically typed, multi-paradigm language created by Larry Wall and first released in 1987; particularly strong in text processing, regular expressions, scripting, reporting, and systems glue.

entities.name: Larry Wall
entities.description: Creator and principal original designer of Perl; his linguistic background influenced Perl's emphasis on expressive, human-oriented syntax.

entities.name: Perl 1
entities.description: Initial public Perl release on December 18, 1987.

entities.name: Perl 2
entities.description: 1988 release that improved the regular-expression engine.

entities.name: Perl 3
entities.description: 1989 release that added binary data-stream support.

entities.name: Perl 4
entities.description: 1991 release associated with the Programming Perl reference book and capitalization of the language name.

entities.name: Perl 5
entities.description: Major rewrite released in 1994, adding references, lexical variables, objects, and modules; remains the main Perl language line.

entities.name: Perl 5.6
entities.description: 2000 release with 64-bit support, Unicode string representation, large-file support, and the our keyword.

entities.name: Perl 5.8
entities.description: 2002 release improving Unicode, I/O, threads, numeric accuracy, and core modules.

entities.name: Perl 5.10
entities.description: 2007 release with regex enhancements, given/when switch-like syntax, and smart match.

entities.name: Perl 5.12
entities.description: 2010 release with features including package NAME VERSION syntax, implicit strictures, Y2038 work, and Unicode updates.

entities.name: Perl 5.14
entities.description: 2011 release with JSON support built into the core distribution.

entities.name: Perl 5.20
entities.description: 2014 release with subroutine signatures, hash slices and new slice syntax, and other language updates.

entities.name: Perl 5.44.0
entities.description: Stable release reported by the supplied source as dated July 15, 2026.

entities.name: Perl 5.45.3
entities.description: Preview release reported by the supplied source as dated September 24, 2026.

entities.name: Raku
entities.description: Language formerly called Perl 6; renamed in October 2019 and developed independently from Perl 5, while ideas may be shared.

entities.name: Perl 6
entities.description: Name used for the redesign effort begun around 2000; renamed Raku in 2019.

entities.name: Perl 7
entities.description: Successor plan announced in 2020, revised in 2021, and later cancelled as a release plan pending sufficient changes.

entities.name: PEARL
entities.description: An existing language whose name led Larry Wall to change the proposed name Pearl to Perl.

entities.name: Unix
entities.description: Original environment and scripting context for Perl's creation.

entities.name: C
entities.description: Language from which Perl borrows broad procedural structure and in which the core interpreter is implemented.

entities.name: AWK
entities.description: Influence on Perl associative arrays/hashes and text-processing idioms.

entities.name: sed
entities.description: Stream editor whose regular-expression and text-transformation ideas influenced Perl.

entities.name: Unix shell
entities.description: Influence on Perl scripting, command invocation, and variable interpolation into strings.

entities.name: BASIC
entities.description: One of the languages listed as influencing Perl.

entities.name: C++
entities.description: Influence listed for Perl and an example compiled language used for performance comparisons.

entities.name: Lisp
entities.description: Influence associated with expression-oriented constructs and implicit return of the final value in a block.

entities.name: JavaScript
entities.description: Language listed among those influenced by Perl.

entities.name: Python
entities.description: Language listed among those influenced by Perl and a comparison point for interpreted-language startup behavior.

entities.name: PHP
entities.description: Language listed among those influenced by Perl and an alternative in web application stacks.

entities.name: Ruby
entities.description: Language listed among those influenced by Perl and a comparison point for interpreted execution.

entities.name: PowerShell
entities.description: Language listed among those influenced by Perl.

entities.name: CoffeeScript
entities.description: Language listed by the source as potentially influenced by Perl; source marks this claim citation-needed.

entities.name: Groovy
entities.description: Language listed by the source as potentially influenced by Perl; source marks this claim citation-needed.

entities.name: Julia
entities.description: Language listed among those influenced by Perl.

entities.name: LPC
entities.description: Language listed among those influenced by Perl.

entities.name: Perl philosophy: TMTOWTDI
entities.description: There's More Than One Way To Do It: Perl often provides multiple ways to express a solution.

entities.name: Easy things easy, hard things possible
entities.description: Perl design slogan emphasizing low friction for common tasks while retaining expressive power.

entities.name: No built-in limits
entities.description: Design ideal favoring flexible data and operations rather than arbitrary small limits.

entities.name: Linguistic design influence
entities.description: Perl syntax reflects linguistic ideas such as making common constructions concise and placing important information prominently.

entities.name: Practicality
entities.description: Perl's culture and design prioritize getting practical jobs done, even when the language accumulates exceptions and heuristics.

entities.name: Perl interpreter
entities.description: Core implementation written in C, coordinating a custom lexer and modified parser, constructing and optimizing syntax trees, and executing programs.

entities.name: Perl C API
entities.description: C-facing collection of structures, macros, typedefs, and functions representing Perl values and operations.

entities.name: Perl compile phase
entities.description: Phase in which Perl source is parsed into a syntax tree and compile-time code may execute.

entities.name: Perl run phase
entities.description: Phase in which the interpreter normally executes the syntax tree, although additional compilation can occur at run time.

entities.name: Syntax tree
entities.description: Tree constructed from parsed Perl code, optimized and then traversed during execution.

entities.name: Modified GNU Bison parser
entities.description: Parser component coordinated with Perl's custom lexer to resolve Perl syntax ambiguities.

entities.name: Custom Perl lexer
entities.description: Lexer used by Perl to coordinate with parsing and compile-time behavior that cannot be handled by a straightforward Lex/Yacc combination.

entities.name: Compile-time execution
entities.description: Perl can execute code during compilation, including code in BEGIN blocks.

entities.name: BEGIN block
entities.description: Block whose code runs during the compile phase.

entities.name: eval
entities.description: Built-in that can compile a string of Perl code at run time, entering compilation during execution.

entities.name: Constant folding
entities.description: Compile-time optimization that evaluates constant expressions in the syntax tree.

entities.name: Context propagation
entities.description: Compile-time optimization listed among Perl syntax-tree transformations.

entities.name: Peephole optimization
entities.description: Local optimization performed by the Perl interpreter.

entities.name: Turing-complete grammar
entities.description: Perl parsing can be affected by code executed during the compile phase, making general parsing theoretically unusual.

entities.name: Halting problem
entities.description: Undecidable problem relevant to the theoretical limits of determining whether arbitrary compile-time code terminates.

entities.name: PPI
entities.description: Project by Adam Kennedy that parses Perl source as a document, preserving source integrity rather than attempting to execute all language semantics.

entities.name: Perl functional test suite
entities.description: Large suite of tests for core Perl and modules used during normal builds to detect regressions.

entities.name: Dynamic typing
entities.description: Perl determines and converts data types at run time, with legal conversions performed automatically.

entities.name: Automatic memory management
entities.description: Interpreter allocates and frees storage for data objects automatically.

entities.name: Reference counting
entities.description: Memory-management technique described for Perl values; circular references may prevent automatic deallocation without intervention.

entities.name: Circular reference
entities.description: Reference cycle that reference counting alone cannot reclaim automatically.

entities.name: Regular expressions
entities.description: Built-in pattern-matching and text-processing facility central to Perl's historical popularity.

entities.name: Regex engine
entities.description: Component improved in Perl 2 and further enhanced in later releases.

entities.name: Regex /x modifier
entities.description: Allows whitespace and formatting in regular expressions to make complex patterns more readable.

entities.name: qr//
entities.description: Perl 5.005 regular-expression quote operator.

entities.name: Strings
entities.description: Scalar string values, with interpolation in appropriate string forms.

entities.name: String interpolation
entities.description: Substitution of variable values into interpolating strings, influenced by shell scripting.

entities.name: Scalars
entities.description: Single-value Perl variables accessed with the $ sigil.

entities.name: Arrays
entities.description: Ordered collections conventionally accessed with the @ sigil; individual elements use scalar access.

entities.name: Hashes
entities.description: Associative arrays mapping keys to values, conventionally accessed with the % sigil.

entities.name: References
entities.description: Perl 5 feature enabling references to values and complex nested data structures.

entities.name: Subroutines
entities.description: Named or anonymous callable blocks used to organize and reuse Perl code.

entities.name: Closures
entities.description: First-class functions that can retain access to lexically scoped variables.

entities.name: Lexical variables
entities.description: Variables declared with lexical scope, especially using my.

entities.name: my
entities.description: Declares lexically scoped variables.

entities.name: our
entities.description: Keyword added in Perl 5.6 for package variables visible through lexical declaration.

entities.name: strict pragma
entities.description: Compiler directive that enables stricter checks to prevent common mistakes.

entities.name: warnings pragma
entities.description: Compiler directive that requests warnings about potentially problematic code.

entities.name: Pragmas
entities.description: Compile-time directives that alter language behavior or checks, such as strict and warnings.

entities.name: Packages
entities.description: Named namespaces that organize symbols and provide a basis for Perl 5 object-oriented conventions.

entities.name: Modules
entities.description: Reusable Perl or C packages loadable by programs; Perl 5 module support enabled language extension without changing the interpreter.

entities.name: CPAN
entities.description: Comprehensive Perl Archive Network, established in 1995, hosting public Perl modules and distributions.

entities.name: Perl module authoring
entities.description: Creating reusable packages that extend applications and often distribute through CPAN.

entities.name: Prototypes
entities.description: Perl 5.002 feature allowing subroutines to influence call syntax similarly to built-ins.

entities.name: Objects
entities.description: Perl 5 introduced support for objects, using references, packages, and method dispatch conventions.

entities.name: Object-oriented programming in Perl
entities.description: Perl 5 object model built from references, packages, and class-based method dispatch.

entities.name: Class-based method dispatch
entities.description: Method calls dispatched according to Perl package/class conventions.

entities.name: Introspection
entities.description: Ability to inspect program and runtime information.

entities.name: Automatic data typing
entities.description: Interpreter tracks data-object type and storage requirements and performs legal conversions at run time.

entities.name: Expressions
entities.description: Perl expressions produce values and can be used within larger expressions.

entities.name: Statements
entities.description: Imperative operations and control statements; blocks use braces.

entities.name: Blocks
entities.description: Brace-delimited groupings of Perl statements; final value may be implicitly returned in relevant contexts.

entities.name: Control structures
entities.description: Conditional and looping structures in Perl.

entities.name: Subroutine signatures
entities.description: Feature noted in Perl 5.20 that allows declaring subroutine parameters.

entities.name: given/when
entities.description: Switch-like syntax introduced in Perl 5.10, with historical/version-dependent status.

entities.name: Smart match operator
entities.description: The ~~ operator introduced in Perl 5.10; behavior is context- and version-sensitive.

entities.name: Sigils
entities.description: Leading characters such as $, @, and % that indicate the kind of variable access/expression in Perl.

entities.name: $ sigil
entities.description: Sigil used for scalar values and individual elements of arrays or hashes.

entities.name: @ sigil
entities.description: Sigil conventionally used for arrays and list-valued access.

entities.name: % sigil
entities.description: Sigil conventionally used for hashes.

entities.name: Context sensitivity
entities.description: Perl built-ins can behave differently in list and scalar contexts.

entities.name: Scalar context
entities.description: Context in which an expression is expected to yield a scalar value.

entities.name: List context
entities.description: Context in which an expression is expected to yield a list of values.

entities.name: Implicit return value
entities.description: The last evaluated value in a block or subroutine can be returned implicitly.

entities.name: File handles
entities.description: Perl values used to represent I/O streams.

entities.name: STDOUT
entities.description: Standard output stream, used by print and for output examples.

entities.name: ARGV
entities.description: Array containing command-line arguments passed to a Perl program.

entities.name: Special variables
entities.description: Built-in variables, some of whose names use punctuation and carry implicit interpreter state.

entities.name: English module
entities.description: Module offering English names for many punctuation-style special variables.

entities.name: Command-line one-liners
entities.description: Compact Perl programs invoked directly from a shell for file and text transformations.

entities.name: Shebang
entities.description: Interpreter-selection line such as #!/usr/bin/env perl at the top of an executable script.

entities.name: Plain Old Documentation (POD)
entities.description: Documentation format associated with Perl; .pod is among Perl-related file extensions.

entities.name: Perl source extensions
entities.description: Common extensions include .pl, .pm, .t, .pod, .cgi, .psgi, .xs, .plx, and .pls.

entities.name: CGI
entities.description: Common Gateway Interface; Perl's regex and text-processing facilities helped make it popular for CGI scripting in the 1990s.

entities.name: PSGI
entities.description: Perl web server gateway interface; .psgi is a Perl-related file extension.

entities.name: mod_perl
entities.description: Apache integration that reduces repeated interpreter startup costs for Perl web applications.

entities.name: ISAPI
entities.description: Microsoft interface through which ActivePerl offered performance improvements.

entities.name: Database Interface (DBI)
entities.description: Database-independent Perl API that lets applications use a common interface for database operations.

entities.name: Database Driver (DBD)
entities.description: Driver modules that implement DBI access to particular database systems.

entities.name: SQL
entities.description: Relational database query language that Perl applications can generate and submit.

entities.name: DBIx::Class
entities.description: Perl ORM often used above DBI to generate SQL and hide database details.

entities.name: Class::DBI
entities.description: Perl ORM named in the source as an abstraction over DBI.

entities.name: Rose::DB::Object
entities.description: Perl ORM named in the source as an abstraction over DBI.

entities.name: Perl/Tk
entities.description: Toolkit commonly used to add graphical interfaces to Perl scripts.

entities.name: wxPerl
entities.description: Perl bindings for wxWidgets commonly used to add graphical interfaces.

entities.name: Inline
entities.description: Module family allowing critical routines to be implemented in another language such as C.

entities.name: XS
entities.description: Flexible Perl extension mechanism for connecting Perl code with C implementations.

entities.name: C extension modules
entities.description: C-based modules can implement performance-critical routines or expose native libraries to Perl.

entities.name: Glue language
entities.description: Role in which Perl connects systems and interfaces not originally designed to interoperate.

entities.name: Data munging
entities.description: Converting, cleaning, parsing, and transforming large amounts of data, often to produce reports.

entities.name: System administration
entities.description: Common Perl use for automation and maintenance of operating systems and services.

entities.name: Network programming
entities.description: Application area listed for Perl.

entities.name: Finance
entities.description: Application area listed for Perl.

entities.name: Bioinformatics
entities.description: Application area listed for Perl.

entities.name: Report generation
entities.description: Original motivating use case for Perl: making report processing easier.

entities.name: Build and deployment scripts
entities.description: Portable scripts used to package, build, and deploy software.

entities.name: Web applications
entities.description: Perl applications historically included CGI systems and web platforms.

entities.name: GUI applications
entities.description: Graphical applications can be built with Perl/Tk or wxPerl.

entities.name: LAMP stack
entities.description: Web development stack where Perl can be used as an alternative to PHP or Python.

entities.description: Project listed as a large Perl-based CGI-era project.

entities.description: Project listed as a large Perl-based CGI-era project.

entities.description: Website named in the source among those using Perl extensively.

entities.description: Website named in the source among those using Perl extensively.

entities.description: Project listed as a large Perl-based project.

entities.description: Project listed as a large Perl-based project.

entities.description: Closed-source distribution from ActiveState described in the source as tracking core Perl releases.

entities.name: MacPerl
entities.description: Special Perl port shipped independently for classic Mac OS.

entities.name: POSIX
entities.description: Operating-system standard whose compliant platforms are described as generally supporting compilation of Perl.

entities.name: Artistic License 1.0
entities.description: One of the two licenses under which Perl is distributed.

entities.name: GNU General Public License
entities.description: Alternative license for Perl; the source states version 1 or any later version.

entities.name: Programming Perl
entities.description: O'Reilly reference book published in 1991; its camel cover led to the common name Camel Book.

entities.name: Camel Book
entities.description: Common nickname for Programming Perl, derived from the camel on its cover.

entities.name: O'Reilly Media
entities.description: Publisher of Programming Perl and owner of the camel image trademark described in the source.

entities.name: Camel symbol
entities.description: Unofficial Perl symbol popularized by Programming Perl's camel cover.

entities.name: Perl Foundation
entities.description: Organization that owns the onion symbol and supports community activities.

entities.name: Onion logo
entities.description: Alternative Perl symbol owned by The Perl Foundation; a visual pun on pearl onion.

entities.name: New camel logo (2024)
entities.description: Non-official camel logo published in 2024 under a Creative Commons license by a small developer group.

entities.name: Comprehensive Perl Archive Network (CPAN)
entities.description: Repository and ecosystem for Perl modules and distributions, established October 26, 1995.

entities.name: perl5-porters
entities.description: Mailing list established in 1994 to coordinate Perl 5 porting and continuing development.

entities.name: Perl Mongers
entities.description: Community network whose user groups helped originate the YAPC conference series.

entities.name: PerlMonks
entities.description: Online community mentioned as a venue for Perl poetry and Perl-related exchange.

entities.name: State of the Onion
entities.description: Larry Wall's yearly keynote-style summaries of Perl development and community.

entities.name: YAPC
entities.description: Yet Another Perl Conference, a community conference series begun in 1999; later names included The Perl Conference and The Perl and Raku Conference.

entities.name: The Perl Journal Obfuscated Perl Contest
entities.description: Contest held from 1996 to 2000 celebrating syntactic flexibility and deliberately obfuscated Perl code.

entities.name: JAPH
entities.description: Just Another Perl Hacker short programs, often compact or obfuscated, that print a signature phrase.

entities.name: Perl golf
entities.description: Challenge of minimizing character count in Perl programs.

entities.name: Perl poetry
entities.description: Poems that are also syntactically valid Perl programs.

entities.name: Black Perl
entities.description: Known example of Perl poetry.

entities.name: Perl language specification
entities.description: The source states that Perl 5 has no separately written formal language standard; interpreter behavior and tests serve as a de facto specification.

entities.name: Perl functional tests
entities.description: Functional tests distributed with Perl and run during the normal build process.

entities.name: Interpreter startup overhead
entities.description: Perl source is compiled on each execution, which can make short-lived programs slower to start than comparable compiled programs.

entities.name: Bytecode interpretation
entities.description: Execution overhead noted for Perl relative to compiled languages.

entities.name: Dynamic type checking overhead
entities.description: Run-time type checks contribute to execution overhead.

entities.name: Memory usage
entities.description: Benchmark implementations of Perl often use relatively high memory compared with some alternatives.

entities.name: Benchmarking Game
entities.description: Computer Language Benchmarks Game used to compare implementations of typical programming tasks.

entities.name: Perl version emulation
entities.description: Feature added in Perl 5.16 to request behavior associated with a specified Perl version.

entities.name: Unicode support
entities.description: Perl's Unicode support improved significantly in Perl 5.6 and later releases.

entities.name: 64-bit support
entities.description: Perl 5.6 added 64-bit support.

entities.name: Binary data streams
entities.description: Perl 3 added support for binary data streams.

entities.name: Large-file support
entities.description: Perl 5.6 added support for files larger than 2 GiB.

entities.name: Thread support
entities.description: Perl 5.8 included a new thread implementation.

entities.name: JSON support
entities.description: JSON support is described as built into the core starting with Perl 5.14.

entities.name: CGI.pm
entities.description: Module included in Perl 5.004 that contributed to Perl's popularity as a CGI scripting language.

entities.name: UNIVERSAL package
entities.description: Perl 5.004 addition providing a base object from which classes are automatically derived.

entities.name: Perl On New Internal Engine (PONIE)
entities.description: 2003–2006 effort to bridge Perl 5 and Perl 6 by targeting the Parrot virtual machine; discontinued.

entities.name: Parrot VM
entities.description: Cross-language virtual machine selected in 2001 as a planned Perl 6 runtime and target of PONIE.

entities.name: Pugs
entities.description: Perl 6 implementation and exploration platform written in Haskell by Audrey Tang, started in 2005.

entities.name: Rakudo
entities.description: Implementation of Perl 6/Raku described as an active implementation in the source's historical account.

entities.name: MoarVM
entities.description: C-based virtual machine designed primarily for Rakudo, announced in 2013.

entities.name: Niecza
entities.description: Historical Perl 6 implementation targeting the Common Language Runtime.

entities.name: Common Language Runtime
entities.description: Runtime targeted by the historical Niecza implementation.

entities.name: Java Virtual Machine
entities.description: Runtime considered for Perl 6; source notes this approach was found problematic for the design, while historical implementations had support.

entities.name: Perl 6 RFCs
entities.description: Community submitted more than 300 requests for comments to guide the Perl 6 redesign.

entities.name: Apocalypses
entities.description: Larry Wall's numbered documents describing and organizing Perl 6 design changes.

entities.name: Synopses
entities.description: Documents that evolved into the Perl 6 language specification.

entities.name: Modern Perl
entities.description: Style/movement emphasizing CPAN, newer language features, and high-quality code.

entities.name: Modern Perl book
entities.description: Book associated with the Modern Perl movement.

entities.name: CGI scripting
entities.description: Perl's historic web use, boosted by text processing and regular expressions.

entities.name: Text processing
entities.description: Core Perl capability for searching, extracting, transforming, and reporting textual data.

entities.name: Hash slices
entities.description: Feature noted in Perl 5.20.

entities.name: Y2038 compliance
entities.description: Perl 5.12 core enhancement described as full Y2038 compliance.

entities.name: DTrace support
entities.description: Tracing support included in Perl 5.12 and further hooks in 5.18.

entities.name: Security release
entities.description: Perl 5.003 was released as a security release.

entities.name: Cross-platform portability
entities.description: Perl distributions are available for many operating systems, particularly Unix-like platforms.

entities.name: Perl documentation
entities.description: Documentation historically included a lengthy man page and later extensive perldoc material.

entities.name: Perldoc
entities.description: Documentation system and collection of Perl manuals.

entities.name: Perl culture
entities.description: Practical, humorous, collaborative culture expressed through conferences, JAPH, golf, poetry, and other traditions.

entities.name: Perl 5 module system
entities.description: Reusable module mechanism introduced in Perl 5 that permits language extension outside the interpreter core.

entities.name: Linguistic heuristics
entities.description: Heuristics and tolerated exceptions used to resolve Perl syntactic ambiguities.

entities.name: Ambiguous syntax
entities.description: Some Perl constructs require parser and lexer coordination due to context and compile-time behavior.

entities.name: Write-only language criticism
entities.description: Criticism that Perl syntax can be difficult to read; source notes that careful style and formatted regexes can mitigate it.

entities.name: Line noise criticism
entities.description: Description of Perl punctuation-heavy syntax, especially special variables and regular expressions.

entities.name: perlstyle
entities.description: Perl style documentation recommending readable code and discussing techniques such as the regex /x modifier.

entities.name: perlfunc
entities.description: Manual page documenting Perl built-in functions, including context-dependent behavior.

entities.name: perlintro
entities.description: Introductory Perl document that discusses punctuation-style special variables.

entities.name: File I/O
entities.description: Perl's I/O implementation was improved in Perl 5.8.

entities.name: Networking and OS calls
entities.description: Built-ins provide access to sorting and operating-system facilities commonly needed in scripts.

entities.name: Perl command-line options -i -n -p -l -e
entities.description: Options used in one-liners for in-place editing, implicit input loops, printing, line-ending handling, and inline program code.
